podcasts.title: Why the Agent Era Needs a New Operating System | DHH
podcasts.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson thinks the agent era is reopening a window in computing that has been closed for decades: the chance to build a new operating system people actually want to use. DHH joins a16z General Partners Martin Casado and Anish Acharya to explain why he’s building Omarchy, an agent-first Linux distribution designed around a computer that users can modify simply by asking. They discuss why the command lines, config files, and detailed error messages that once made Linux intimidating now make it unusually well suited to agents, and why DHH believes software development has become cheap enough to challenge decades-old platform lock-in. But if code is becoming abundant, what still matters? DHH argues that taste, craft, and the willingness to obsess over the final 2% become more important, not less. The conversation moves from tiny teams wielding the productive capacity of thousands of people to open models, competition at the frontier, and the return of hacker, demo, and pseudonymous internet culture. podcasts.title: How Fast Should We Build Superintelligence? | Nick Bostrom
podcasts.summary: The question isn’t simply whether humanity should race toward superintelligence or stop. Nick Bostrom argues the harder challenge is preserving the ability to slow down when safety falls behind, without turning a temporary pause into permanent technological stagnation. a16z’s Eddy Lazzarin and Elena Burger sit down with Bostrom to revisit the ideas he helped bring into the mainstream, now that increasingly capable AI systems actually exist. They discuss why alignment may become harder as models grow more situationally aware, which capability improvements may carry more risk than others, and why Bostrom favors “pacing the frontier” rather than committing to a broad or indefinite pause. They also examine the cost of waiting. Bostrom argues that safely developed superintelligence could radically extend human lifespans and address problems from disease to poverty, meaning delay carries risks of its own. From there, the conversation turns to Deep Utopia , governance, the possibility of post-human forms of life, the simulation argument, and whether AI could eventually surpass humans at philosophy itself. podcasts.title: Superintelligence Needs the Physical World with CEO and Co-Founder of Arda Bob McGrew
podcasts.summary: Is the AI singularity actually coming? Bob McGrew, former Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, argues that superintelligence won’t arrive without changes in the physical world, and that the “hard takeoff” argument is wrong. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with Bob, an early key executive at Palantir who later led research at OpenAI. He is now CEO and co-founder of Arda, which is leveraging AI to make American manufacturing competitive. Bob explains why automating AI researchers is a one-time boost rather than a runaway loop, and why GPUs, compute, wet labs, and factories are the real bottlenecks. They cover Arda’s work with Anduril on everything from actuators to missiles to the Fury combat aircraft, why Arda is building “Cursor for manufacturing engineers”, and how the forward deployed engineering model really works. Plus, the big-picture future view: machines that make machines, self-replicating factories, and Bob’s answer to the Fermi paradox. Sign up for new podcasts every week. podcasts.summary: My guests today are Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital, and Geoffrey Canada, founder of Harlem Children's Zone. Geoffrey spent decades helping disadvantaged kids get a great education, but it takes more than that to achieve the American dream. Without savings, you’re one emergency away from bankruptcy. Brad set out to change that. When he first called me about Invest America in 2020, I thought it was a fool’s errand. Six years later, nearly 70 million children have accounts in their name, and every American newborn receives $1,000 in the S&P 500. The challenge now is getting families to claim their accounts, since free money is surprisingly hard to give away. Brad and Geoffrey believe even a small nest egg, when given a head start on compounding, can help rebuild faith in capitalism. As AI reshapes the economy, they see these accounts as the basis of a new social contract built on ownership and participation, where every child owns a piece of the upside. podcasts.title: USA v/s China AI Labs. OpenSource AI after Jensen leaves NVIDIA
podcasts.summary: More than 1.5 GW of chips are in China that shouldn’t be. Unwinding that web could reshape open-source AI. “In our view, there’s more than one and a half gigawatts of chips in China that are not supposed to be there according to US law. How they get there, that whole web, that’s what’s going to unwind.” “If NVIDIA can no longer support the open-source ecosystem, because that was Jensen’s primary goal, does that mean the open-source ecosystem falls away?” “Now open source looks a lot weaker with NVIDIA down and out. Anthropic looks much more likely to get a complete monopoly or a duopoly. This bodes really well for Anthropic’s IPO next week.” “They’re more diverse in what chips they use than any other company in the world.”

We close with Paul's approach to managing his own money and his answers to a terrific set of questions sourced from his Twitter feed before the show. podcasts.title: The devil’s advocate case for letting China rent American compute.
podcasts.summary: The devil’s advocate case for letting China rent American compute. “If China has access to compute outside of China, it’s paying humongous margin dollars to the US ecosystem. Nvidia makes about $7 million of profit on every megawatt deployed. The cloud provider makes another $7 to 10 million at today’s pricing.” “If ByteDance wants to compete with Meta on video recommendation globally, and you don’t let it buy the chips but you do let it rent them, Meta potentially has a fourth of the cost of compute.” “Application-layer companies running on open models add up to well north of $10 billion in ARR. DeepSeek makes less than Baseten and Fireworks do serving its models. America is making so much money off Chinese models.” Watch the Full Podcast on YouTube.
